GeSn/Ge multiple quantum-well p-i-n phototectors with low Sn-fraction can be used to detect long-wavelength infrared light.
GeSn/Ge photodetectors can achieve a high quantum efficiency and detectivity, and that this is possible with Ge0.964/0.036Sn active layers.

we have demonstrated the possibility of developing GeSn/ Ge-based p-i-n photovoltaic infrared photodetctors with a 2.0-2.1 μ cut-off wavelength and a high responsivity at a 1550-nm wavelength peak, by using a Ge0.964Sno.036/Ge active layer with a 0.036 Sn fraction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed theoretical investigation of the performance of GeSn/Ge photodetectors, which are promising candidates for infrared photodetection in the 1.5-2.5 μm range.
the development of a GeSn/Ge photodiode for mid-infrared applications.
the development of high-detectivities GeSn/Ge photodetectors for the 1.55 μmm band.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GeSn/Ge photodetector with low Sn fraction can be a promising candidate for mid-infrared photodetectors.
the GeSn/Ge photodetector with a low Sn fraction of 3.6% is an excellent alternative to the conventional Ge photodetector.

the compressively-strained p-i-n phototransistors with the GeSn/Ge MQW active region are promising candidates for the future infrared photodetection applications, particularly for the Ge-based integrated optoelectronics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GeSn/Ge multiple quantum-well infrared photodetctor (MWIP) has a high responsivity, a high detectivity and a low dark current.
we can achieve a Ge0.964 Sn0.036/ Ge p-i-n photodevice with a high detectivity of 3 × 1010 Jones at room temperature and with a cut-off wavelength of 2.1μm.
the Ge0.964 Sn0.036/ Ge p-i-n phototransistor is a promising candidate for infrared detection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Ge1−xSnx/Ge heterostructures are promising for the development of infrared photodetected with practical Sn fractions.
GeSn/Ge photodiodes with practical GeSn active layer composition can have excellent detectivity, which is comparable to or even better than those of pure-Ge devices.
the use of compressively-strained quantum wells in GeSn/Ge heterostructures can lead to a significant enhancement in the photodetectors’ performance, even for low Sn-fraction GeSn layers.
